name: Sensor Dashboard
description: Register sensors, record their readings and watch the latest values and recent history on a dashboard
backend_requirements: Access control: anyone may read sensors and their readings; require auth for registering and deleting sensors and for posting readings, and only the user who registered a sensor may post readings to it or delete it (403 otherwise); admin endpoints are restricted to the admin account

Sensor validation: name is a required non-empty string of at most 100 characters, unit a required non-empty string of at most 20 characters (for example C, %, hPa), location an optional string of at most 100 characters
Readings: POST /api/sensors/:id/readings stores a numeric value with the current time as recorded_at and makes it the sensor's last_value and last_updated; a missing or non-numeric value answers 400
A new sensor has last_value and last_updated null until its first reading
GET /api/sensors lists active sensors sorted by name, each with owner (the registering user's username), last_value and last_updated
GET /api/sensors/:id/readings lists a sensor's readings newest first; ?limit= caps how many are returned (default 50, at most 500) while total counts all of the sensor's readings
DELETE /api/sensors/:id removes the sensor and its readings permanently
Deactivated sensors (is_active false) are left out of GET /api/sensors, answer 404 on the public sensor endpoints and accept no readings; the admin overview still lists them
Errors answer with a JSON object {"detail": "<message>"}: 400 for invalid input, 401 without a valid token, 403 for another user's sensor or a non-admin on admin endpoints, 404 for unknown ids
frontend_requirements: Everyone sees the sensor dashboard and sensor details read-only; signed-in users also get the register-sensor form and, on their own sensors, the record-reading and delete controls, and visitors see a 'Sign in to register sensors' prompt in their place
Sign-in and registration forms that call /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register; keep the token for later requests, show the signed-in username and offer sign-out
Dashboard: one card per sensor with name, location, last value with its unit and how long ago it was updated; it polls the API every 10 seconds and also has a manual refresh button
Sensor detail view: the sensor's fields and a line chart plus a table of its recent readings
Register-sensor and record-reading forms that show the API's validation messages next to the form; delete asks for confirmation first
An empty state that explains how to register the first sensor when there are none
admin_requirements: Admin overview: every sensor, active or not, with total, active and inactive counts and the total number of readings
Toggle a sensor's active status from the overview

api_endpoints.description: List active sensors by name with their latest value
Register a sensor owned by the signed-in user
Delete one of your sensors and its readings
Readings of a sensor, newest first

query.limit: How many of the newest readings to return (default 50, at most 500)

api_endpoints.description: Record a reading for one of your sensors

data_models.name: Sensor
data_models.description: A registered sensor; last_value and last_updated mirror its newest reading

fields.user_id: integer (references the signed-in user who registered it)
fields.name: string (required, max 100 chars)
fields.last_updated: datetime (null until the first reading, ISO 8601 in JSON)
fields.is_active: boolean (default true; false hides the sensor from public endpoints)

data_models.name: Reading
data_models.description: One recorded value of a sensor

fields.sensor_id: integer (references Sensor.id; deleted with the sensor)

admin_api_endpoints.description: Admin overview: every sensor with counts
